translations.literal: Treatise twenty-one: Commanderies and States, part three.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 21: “Commanderies and States,” Part Three.

sentences.zh: 陈留 东郡 东平 任城 泰山 济北 山阳 济阴

translations.literal: Chenliu, Dong, Dongping, Rencheng, Taishan, Jibei, Shanyang, Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: This section treats Chenliu, Dong, Dongping, Rencheng, Taishan, Jibei, Shanyang, and Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 东海 琅邪 彭城 广陵 下邳

translations.literal: Donghai, Langye, Pengcheng, Guangling, Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: It also covers Donghai, Langye, Pengcheng, Guangling, and Xiapi.

translations.literal: The Chenliu commandery was established by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu Commandery was first set up under Emperor Wu of Han.

translations.literal: Five hundred thirty li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Its seat lay about five hundred thirty li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十七城，户十七万七千五百二十九，口八十六万九千四百三十三。

translations.literal: Seventeen walled places; 177,729 households; 869,433 persons.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery comprised seventeen county seats, 177,729 households, and 869,433 people.

translations.literal: Chenliu: it had the Mingyan pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenliu there was Mingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 〖浚仪〗本大梁。帝王世記曰：「禹避商均浚儀。」晉地道記：「儀封人，此縣也。」通俗文曰「渠在浚儀，曰莨蕩」也。

translations.literal: Junyi: originally Daliang. The Diwang shiji says, “Yu avoided Shangjun at Junyi.” The Jin didao ji says, “The man of Yifeng was from this county.” The Tongsu wen says, “The canal at Junyi is called Langdang.”
translations.idiomatic: Junyi had been Daliang. The Diwang shiji says, “Yu avoided Shangjun at Junyi.” The Jin didao ji says, “The man of Yifeng was from this county.” The Tongsu wen says, “The canal at Junyi is called Langdang.”

sentences.zh: 〖尉氏〗陳留志曰：「有陵樹鄕，北有澤，澤有天子菀囿，有秦樂廄，漢諸帝以馴養猛獸。」

translations.literal: Weishi: the Chenliu zhi says, “It had Lingshu Township. To the north was a marsh; in the marsh were the Son of Heaven’s park and enclosure, and there was the Qin music stable. The Han emperors used it to tame and raise fierce beasts.”
translations.idiomatic: Weishi: the Chenliu zhi says, “It had Lingshu Township. North of it was a marsh containing the Son of Heaven’s park and enclosure, as well as the Qin music stable. The Han emperors used it to train and keep fierce beasts.”

sentences.zh: 〖雍丘〗本杞国。陳留志曰：「城内有神井，能興霧雹。」案：徐齊民北征記曰：「有呂祿臺，髙七丈。有酈生祠。」曹植禹廟讚曰：「有禹祠，植移於其城，城本名杞城。」

translations.literal: Yongqiu: originally the state of Qi. The Chenliu zhi says, “Inside the city was a divine well, which could raise fog and hail.” Note: Xu Qimin’s Beizheng ji says, “It had Lü Lu’s Terrace, seven zhang high. It had the shrine of Li Sheng.” Cao Zhi’s Praise of Yu’s Temple says, “There was a shrine to Yu, which Zhi moved into the city; the city was originally named Qi city.”
translations.idiomatic: Yongqiu was the old state of Qi. The Chenliu zhi says, “Inside the city was a divine well that could bring forth fog and hail.” Xu Qimin’s Beizheng ji says, “It had Lü Lu’s Terrace, seven zhang high, and a shrine to Li Sheng.” Cao Zhi’s Praise of Yu’s Temple says, “There was a shrine to Yu, which Zhi moved into the city; the city was originally called Qi city.”

translations.literal: Xiangyi: it had Hua Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyi had Hua Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 有承匡城。地道記曰在縣西。左傳文十一年會晉郤缺於承匡。

translations.literal: It had Chengkuang city. The Didiao ji says it was west of the county. In Duke Wen 11, the Zuo Tradition says they met Jin's Xi Que at Chengkuang.
translations.idiomatic: The same county also contained Chengkuang; the Didiao ji places it west of the county, and the Zuo Tradition records a meeting there with Xi Que of Jin in Duke Wen 11.

sentences.zh: 〖外黄〗左傳「惠公季年，敗宋師於黃」，杜預曰宋邑，縣東有黃城。有葵丘聚，齊桓公會此，城中有曲棘里。左傳昭二十五年「宋公佐卒曲棘」。

translations.literal: Waihuang: the Zuo Tradition says, “In the last year of Duke Hui, he defeated the Song army at Huang”; Du Yu says it was a Song settlement, and east of the county was Huang city. It had Kuiqiu settlement, where Duke Huan of Qi met the lords; inside the city was Quji ward. In Duke Zhao 25, the Zuo Tradition says, “Duke Zuo of Song died at Quji.”
translations.idiomatic: At Waihuang, the Zuo Tradition says, “In the last year of Duke Hui, he defeated the Song army at Huang”; Du Yu identifies Huang as a Song settlement and notes a Huang city east of the county. Waihuang also held Kuiqiu, where Duke Huan of Qi met the other rulers, and Quji ward within the city; the Zuo Tradition records, “Duke Zuo of Song died at Quji,” in Duke Zhao 25.

translations.literal: It had Fanyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang was another fortified place in the county.

sentences.zh: 〖小黃〗漢舊儀曰：「髙祖母起兵時死縣北，爲作陵廟於小黃。」

translations.literal: Xiaohuang: The Old Han Rites says, “When Emperor Gaozu’s mother died north of the county during the uprising, a tomb shrine was made for her at Xiaohuang.”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohuang: The Old Han Rites says, “When Emperor Gaozu’s mother died north of the county during the uprising, a tomb shrine was made for her at Xiaohuang.”

sentences.zh: 〖東昬〗陳留志曰：「故戸牖鄕有陳平祠。」

translations.literal: Donghun: The Chenliu zhi says, “In former Huyou Township there was a shrine to Chen Ping.”
translations.idiomatic: Donghun: The Chenliu zhi says, “In former Huyou Township there was a shrine to Chen Ping.”

sentences.zh: 〖濟陽〗有武父鄕。左傳桓十二年「盟於武父」，杜預曰縣東北有武父城。縣東南有戎城。縣都鄕有行宮，光武生。

translations.literal: Jiyang had Wufu Township. In Duke Huan 12, the Zuo Tradition says, “They covenanted at Wufu”; Du Yu says Wufu City was northeast of the county. Southeast of the county was Rong City. In Du Township of the county there was a temporary palace where Guangwu was born.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyang had Wufu Township. The Zuo Tradition says, “They covenanted at Wufu,” in Duke Huan 12, and Du Yu places Wufu City northeast of the county. Rong City lay southeast of the county, and in Du Township there was a temporary palace where Guangwu was born.

translations.literal: Pingqiu: it had Linji pavilion, where Tian Dan died; it had Kuang; it had Huangchi pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Pingqiu included Linji Pavilion, where Tian Dan met his death, together with Kuang and Huangchi Pavilion.

translations.literal: It had Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: The county also had Kuang.

sentences.zh: 有黄池亭。陳留志云：「黃亭在封丘。」左傳哀十三年盟黃池，杜預曰在〔封邱〕縣南。傳曰「呉囚子服景伯以還，及戸牖」，然卽黃池在戸牖西。或以爲外黃縣東溝，非也。

translations.literal: It had Huangchi Pavilion. The Chenliu zhi says, “Huang Pavilion was in Fengqiu.” In Duke Ai 13 of the Zuo Tradition, there was a covenant at Huangchi; Du Yu says it was south of Fengqiu county. The tradition says, “Wu imprisoned Zifu Jingbo and returned with him, reaching Huyou,” so Huangchi was west of Huyou. Some take it to be the eastern ditch of Waihuang county, but this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchi Pavilion was there. The Chenliu zhi says, “Huang Pavilion was in Fengqiu.” In Duke Ai 13 of the Zuo Tradition, the covenant at Huangchi took place; Du Yu places it south of Fengqiu county. The tradition says, “Wu imprisoned Zifu Jingbo and returned with him, reaching Huyou,” which means Huangchi was west of Huyou. Some identify it with the eastern ditch of Waihuang county, but that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 〖封丘〗博物記有狄溝，卽敗狄於長丘是也。有桐牢亭，或曰古虫牢。左傳成五年諸侯會蟲牢。陳留志：「有鞠亭，古鞠居。」

translations.literal: Fengqiu: the Bowu ji has Di Ditch, which is where the Di were defeated at Changqiu. It had Tonglao Pavilion; some say it was ancient Chonglao. In Duke Cheng 5 of the Zuo Tradition, the lords met at Chonglao. The Chenliu zhi says, “It had Ju Pavilion, the ancient dwelling of Ju.”
translations.idiomatic: Fengqiu: the Bowu ji records Di Ditch, the place where the Di were defeated at Changqiu. It had Tonglao Pavilion, which some identify as ancient Chonglao. In Duke Cheng 5 of the Zuo Tradition, the lords met at Chonglao. The Chenliu zhi says, “It had Ju Pavilion, the old settlement of Ju.”

sentences.zh: 〖酸枣〗左傳鄭太叔至於廩延，杜預曰縣北有延津。襄五年會城棣，杜預曰縣西南有棣城。東有地烏巣，曹公破袁紹處。陳留志曰：「城内有韓王故宮闕。」

translations.literal: Suanzao: in the Zuo Tradition, Taishu of Zheng reached Linyan; Du Yu says Yanjin was north of the county. In Duke Xiang 5, there was a meeting at Chengdi; Du Yu says Di city was southwest of the county. To the east was a place named Wuchao, where Lord Cao defeated Yuan Shao. The Chenliu zhi says, “Inside the city were the old palace gates of the Han kings.”
translations.idiomatic: Suanzao: in the Zuo Tradition, Taishu of Zheng reached Linyan; Du Yu places Yanjin north of the county. In Duke Xiang 5, a meeting was held at Chengdi; Du Yu places Di city southwest of the county. East of the county was Wuchao, where Lord Cao defeated Yuan Shao. The Chenliu zhi says, “Inside the city were the old palace gates of the Han kings.”

translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was organized as a marquisate and contained the settlements of Kuang, Pu, and Ji.

translations.literal: It had Kuang city.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang city stood there.

translations.literal: It had Pu city.
translations.idiomatic: Pu city was in the county.

translations.literal: It had Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: Ji city was also recorded.

translations.literal: Jiwu: it had Daji township; it had Shou township.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwu had Daji Township and Shou Township.

translations.literal: It had Shou township.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Township lay in the same county.

translations.literal: Kaocheng: formerly Zai, renamed by Emperor Zhang; formerly it belonged to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Kaocheng had once been called Zai until Emperor Zhang changed the name; it had belonged to Liang.

translations.literal: Formerly it belonged to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier it was under Liang’s jurisdiction.

translations.literal: Yu: formerly it belonged to Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had previously been part of Huaiyang.

translations.literal: It had Gaoyang pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyang Pavilion was located there.

translations.literal: Fugou: formerly it belonged to Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fugou, too, had once been assigned to Huaiyang.

translations.literal: The Dong commandery was established by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Commandery dated from the Qin founding of the empire.

translations.literal: More than eight hundred li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It lay a little over eight hundred li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十五城，户十三万六千八十八，口六十万三千三百九十三。

translations.literal: Fifteen walled places; 136,088 households; 603,393 persons.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery counted fifteen seats, 136,088 households, and 603,393 inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 〖濮阳〗古昆吾国，杜預曰古衞也。帝王世記曰：「顓頊自窮桑徙商丘。」左傳曰「衞，顓頊之墟」，杜預曰帝丘，昆吾氏因之，故曰昆吾之墟，縣城内有顓頊冢。皇覽曰：「冢在城門外廣陽里中。」博物記曰：「桑中在其中。」春秋时曰濮。

translations.literal: Puyang: the ancient state of Kunwu; Du Yu says it was ancient Wey. The Diwang shiji says, “Zhuanxu moved from Qiongsang to Shangqiu.” The Zuo Tradition says, “Wey was the ruins of Zhuanxu”; Du Yu says this was Diqiu, and the Kunwu clan followed from it, so it was called the ruins of Kunwu. Inside the county city was Zhuanxu's tomb. The Huanglan says, “The tomb was in Guangyang ward outside the city gate.” The Bowu ji says, “Sangzhong was within it.” In the Spring and Autumn period it was called Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Puyang was old Kunwu territory; Du Yu identifies it with ancient Wey. The Diwang shiji says, “Zhuanxu moved from Qiongsang to Shangqiu,” and the Zuo Tradition says, “Wey was the ruins of Zhuanxu.” Du Yu explains that this was Diqiu, from which the Kunwu clan derived, hence the name “ruins of Kunwu”; Zhuanxu's tomb stood inside the county city. The Huanglan says, “The tomb was in Guangyang ward outside the city gate,” and the Bowu ji adds, “Sangzhong was within it.” In Spring and Autumn times the place was called Pu.

translations.literal: It had Xian city; some say it was the ancient state of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: There was Xian city, which some take for the polity of Xian.

translations.literal: It had Qingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qingqiu was another site.

translations.literal: It had Chu city.
translations.idiomatic: The county also held Chu city.

translations.literal: Yan: originally the southern Yan state.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had been the heartland of Southern Yan.

translations.literal: It had Yong township.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Township lay within it.

translations.literal: It had Zuocheng, the ancient state of Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zuocheng preserved the ground of the old state of Zuo.

translations.literal: It had Pingyang pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang Pavilion was noted there.

translations.literal: It had Wa pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Wa Pavilion appears in the gazetteer.

translations.literal: It had Tao city.
translations.idiomatic: Tao city was another landmark.

sentences.zh: 〖白马〗有韦乡。杜預曰：「縣東南有韋城。古豕韋氏之國」。

translations.literal: Baima: it had Wei Township. Du Yu says, “Southeast of the county was Wei city, the ancient state of the Shiwei clan.”
translations.idiomatic: Baima contained Wei Township. Du Yu says, “Southeast of the county stood Wei city, the ancient state of the Shiwei clan.”

sentences.zh: 〖顿丘〗皇覽曰「帝嚳冢在城〔南〕臺陰野〔中〕」是也。

translations.literal: Dunqiu: this is the place where the Huanglan says, “The tomb of Di Ku was in the fields of Taiyin south of the city.”
translations.idiomatic: Dunqiu: this is the place meant by the Huanglan when it says, “The tomb of Di Ku was in the Taiyin fields south of the city.”

sentences.zh: 〖东阿〗左傳桓十年會於桃丘，杜預曰縣東南有桃城。襄十四年孫林父敗衞侯於阿澤，杜預曰縣西南大澤。魏志有渠丘山。有清亭。左傳隱四年「遇於淸」是也。

translations.literal: Dong’e: in Duke Huan 10 of the Zuo Tradition, there was a meeting at Taoqiu; Du Yu says Tao city was southeast of the county. In Duke Xiang 14, Sun Linfu defeated the Marquis of Wei at Aze; Du Yu says this was the great marsh southwest of the county. The Wei zhi has Mount Quqiu. It had Qing Pavilion. This is where the Zuo Tradition says in Duke Yin 4, “They met at Qing.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong’e: in Duke Huan 10 of the Zuo Tradition, a meeting was held at Taoqiu; Du Yu places Tao city southeast of the county. In Duke Xiang 14, Sun Linfu defeated the Marquis of Wei at Aze; Du Yu identifies this with the great marsh southwest of the county. The Wei zhi records Mount Quqiu. Dong’e had Qing Pavilion, the place meant when the Zuo Tradition says in Duke Yin 4, “They met at Qing.”

translations.literal: Dongwuyang: the Shi River issues forth here.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi River rose in Dongwuyang.

translations.literal: Fan: it had Qin pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had Qin Pavilion.

translations.literal: Linyi: it had a shrine to the Marquis of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: At Linyi stood a temple honoring the Marquis of Pei.

translations.literal: Boping.
translations.idiomatic: Boping County.

translations.literal: Liaocheng: it had Yiyi gathering; it had Nie city.
translations.idiomatic: Liaocheng held Yiyi Gathering and Nie city.

translations.literal: It had Nie city.
translations.idiomatic: Nie city was in the county.

translations.literal: Fagan.
translations.idiomatic: Fagan County.

translations.literal: Leping: a marquisate; formerly Qing, renamed by Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Leping was a marquisate once called Qing until Emperor Zhang altered the name.

translations.literal: Formerly Qing, renamed by Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The old name Qing was retired by Emperor Zhang’s edict.

translations.idiomatic: Yangping was a marquisate with Shen Pavilion and Gangcheng city.

translations.literal: It had Shen pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pavilion lay there.

translations.literal: It had Gangcheng city.
translations.idiomatic: Gangcheng city appears in the record.

translations.literal: Wei: a ducal state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was ranked as a ducal fief.

sentences.zh: 本观故国，姚姓，光武更名。

translations.literal: Originally the ancient state of Guan, surname Yao; renamed by Emperor Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: It had been the old polity of Guan, of the Yao lineage, until Emperor Guangwu changed the designation.

translations.literal: It had Hemu city.
translations.idiomatic: Hemu city stood in the state.

translations.literal: It had Gan city.
translations.idiomatic: Gan city was also listed.

translations.literal: Gucheng: in the Spring and Autumn period, Lesser Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng was the “Lesser Gu” of Spring and Autumn annals.

translations.literal: It had Xu Xia gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xia Gathering lay in its territory.

sentences.zh: 东平国故梁，景帝分为济东国，宣帝改。

translations.literal: The Dongping kingdom: formerly Liang; Emperor Jing split it off as the eastern Ji kingdom; Emperor Xuan altered the name.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping had been Liang until Emperor Jing carved out eastern Ji and Emperor Xuan reorganized it into this kingdom.

translations.literal: Nine hundred seventy-five li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital sat about nine hundred seventy-five li east of Luoyang.

translations.idiomatic: Seven county seats, 79,012 households, and 448,270 people fell under its administration.

translations.literal: Wuyan: originally the state of Su, surname Ren; it had Zhang city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan had been Su, ruled by the Ren clan, and still held Zhang city.

translations.literal: It had Zhang city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang city was in the county.

translations.literal: Dongping Lu: in the Warring States era it was called Pinglu; it had Kan pavilion; it had Tangyang pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping Lu was known as Pinglu in the Warring States period and contained Kan and Tangyang pavilions.

translations.literal: It had Kan pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Pavilion was there.

translations.literal: It had Tangyang pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Tangyang Pavilion appears in the same entry.

translations.literal: Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fucheng County.

translations.literal: Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang County.

sentences.zh: 〖寿张〗春秋曰良，汉曰寿良，光武改曰寿张。

translations.literal: Shouzhang: in the Spring and Autumn period called Liang; in Han called Shouliang; Emperor Guangwu changed it to Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhang had read Liang in the chronicles, then Shouliang under Western Han, until Emperor Guangwu fixed the present form.

translations.literal: It had Tang gathering, an old gathering belonging to Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Gathering was an old Dong commandery settlement carried over into this county.

translations.literal: Xuchang: formerly it belonged to Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchang had once been filed under Dong.

translations.literal: It had Zhimi city, the ancient Zhongdu; it had Yanggu city.
translations.idiomatic: It held Zhimi city, identified with ancient Zhongdu, and Yanggu city.

translations.literal: It had Yanggu city.
translations.idiomatic: Yanggu city completed the note.

translations.literal: Ningyang: formerly it belonged to Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Ningyang had previously been part of Taishan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 任城国章帝元和元年，分东平为任城。

translations.literal: The Rencheng kingdom: in the first year of the Yuanhe era of Emperor Zhang, Dongping was divided to form Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 84 CE, the first year of Emperor Zhang’s Yuanhe era, territory was split from Dongping to create the kingdom of Rencheng.

translations.literal: One thousand one hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom lay roughly eleven hundred li east of Luoyang.

translations.idiomatic: Kangfu County.

translations.literal: Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan County.

translations.idiomatic: Taishan Commandery was founded in Emperor Gao’s reign.

translations.literal: One thousand four hundred li east of Luoyang.

translations.idiomatic: Twelve county seats, 8,929 households, and 437,317 people were registered.

translations.idiomatic: Liangfu was a marquisate with Tuqiu Gathering.

translations.idiomatic: Nanwuyang was another marquisate seat.

translations.literal: It had Zhuanyu city.
translations.idiomatic: The old settlement of Zhuanyu lay within it.

translations.literal: Nancheng: formerly it belonged to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng had once been administered from Donghai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 有东阳城。呂氏春秋夏孔甲遊田於東陽萯山。左傳哀八年「克東陽」。襄十九年城武城，杜預曰南城縣。哀十四年司馬牛葬丘輿，杜預曰縣西北有輿城。

translations.literal: It had Dongyang city. The Lüshi chunqiu says that Xia Kong Jia hunted at Mount Fushan in Dongyang. In Duke Ai 8, the Zuo Tradition says, “captured Dongyang.” In Duke Xiang 19, it walled Wucheng, which Du Yu says was Nancheng county. In Duke Ai 14, Sima Niu was buried at Qiuyu; Du Yu says northwest of the county was Yu city.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyang city was listed in the same entry. The Lüshi chunqiu says Xia Kong Jia hunted at Mount Fushan in Dongyang; the Zuo Tradition records in Duke Ai 8 that someone “captured Dongyang.” For the walling of Wucheng in Duke Xiang 19, Du Yu identifies the place as Nancheng county, and for Sima Niu's burial at Qiuyu in Duke Ai 14, he notes Yu city northwest of the county.

sentences.zh: 〖费〗侯国，曹勝封費是酇縣費亭，非此國。故属东海。

translations.literal: Fei: a marquisate. The Fei where Cao Sheng was enfeoffed was Fei Pavilion in Zan county, not this state. Formerly it belonged to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was a marquisate. The Fei where Cao Sheng received his fief was Fei Pavilion in Zan county, not this polity; this Fei had once belonged to Donghai.

sentences.zh: 有祊亭。左傳隱八年鄭歸祊，杜預曰在縣東南。閔二年莒人歸共仲及密，杜預曰縣有密如亭。

translations.literal: It had Beng Pavilion. In Duke Yin 8, the Zuo Tradition says Zheng returned Beng; Du Yu says it was southeast of the county. In Duke Min 2, when the men of Ju returned Gongzhong and Mi, Du Yu says the county had Miru Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The county also recorded Beng Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition says in Duke Yin 8 that Zheng returned Beng, which Du Yu places southeast of the county. In Duke Min 2, when the men of Ju returned Gongzhong and Mi, Du Yu notes Miru Pavilion in the county.

sentences.zh: 有台亭。左傳襄十二年莒圍臺，杜預曰縣南有臺亭。

translations.literal: It had Tai Pavilion. In Duke Xiang 12, the Zuo Tradition says Ju besieged Tai; Du Yu says south of the county was Tai Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Pavilion appears beside it in the gazetteer; the Zuo Tradition records Ju besieging Tai in Duke Xiang 12, and Du Yu places Tai Pavilion south of the county.

translations.literal: Mou: an ancient state.
translations.idiomatic: Mou preserved the memory of an independent polity of old.

sentences.zh: 济北国和帝永元二年，分泰山置。

translations.literal: The Jibei kingdom: in the second year of the Yongyuan era of Emperor He, Taishan was divided to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: In 90 CE, Yongyuan 2 of Emperor He, territory was split from Taishan to found the kingdom of Jibei.

translations.literal: One thousand one hundred fifty li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital lay about eleven hundred fifty li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 五城，户四万五千六百八十九，口二十三万五千八百九十七。

translations.literal: Five walled places; 45,689 households; 235,897 persons.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom comprised five seats, 45,689 households, and 235,897 people.

translations.literal: Lu: it had Pingyin city.
translations.idiomatic: Lu contained Pingyin city.

translations.literal: It had Fang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Gate, the old Qi defensive pass, was located there.

translations.literal: It had Guang ward.
translations.idiomatic: Guang ward appears among its settlements.

translations.literal: It had Mount Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jingzi was another landmark.

translations.literal: It had Mount Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Ao is named in the same list.

translations.literal: It had Qing Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Pavilion stood in the county.

translations.literal: It had the Long Wall reaching to the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: A stretch of the Long Wall ran eastward as far as the sea.

sentences.zh: 〖蛇丘〗有遂鄕。古遂國，左傳莊十三年齊人滅遂。

translations.literal: Sheqiu had Sui Township. This was the ancient state of Sui; in Duke Zhuang 13, the Zuo Tradition says that the men of Qi destroyed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sheqiu had Sui Township. This was the ancient state of Sui; in Duke Zhuang 13, the Zuo Tradition says that the men of Qi destroyed Sui.

sentences.zh: 有下讙亭。左傳桓三年送姜氏於讙。

translations.literal: It had Lower Huan Pavilion. In Duke Huan 3, the Zuo Tradition says Jiangshi was escorted to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: It had Lower Huan Pavilion. In Duke Huan 3, the Zuo Tradition says Jiangshi was escorted to Huan.

sentences.zh: 有鑄鄕城。周武王未及下車，封堯後於鑄。

translations.literal: It had Zhu Township City. Before King Wu of Zhou had even dismounted from his carriage, he enfeoffed Yao’s descendant at Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: It had Zhu Township City. Before King Wu of Zhou had even dismounted from his carriage, he enfeoffed Yao’s descendant at Zhu.

sentences.zh: 左傳有棘地，成公三年叔孫僑如所圍。杜預曰汶水北地有棘鄕。東觀書有芳陘山。

translations.literal: The Zuo Tradition has the place Ji, which Shusun Qiaoru besieged in Duke Cheng 3. Du Yu says that north of the Wen River there was Ji Township. The Dongguan shu says there was Mount Fangxing.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition records the place Ji, besieged by Shusun Qiaoru in Duke Cheng 3. Du Yu says Ji Township lay north of the Wen River. The Dongguan shu also records Mount Fangxing.

translations.literal: Cheng: the native state.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was the kingdom’s own seat of government.

translations.literal: Chiping: originally it belonged to Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chiping had earlier been filed under Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 〖剛〗左傳哀八年齊取闡，杜預曰在縣北，有闡鄕。

translations.literal: Gang: in the eighth year of Duke Ai in the Zuo Tradition, Qi seized Chan; Du Yu says it was north of the county and had Chan township.
translations.idiomatic: For Gang, the note cites the Zuo Tradition and Du Yu: Chan lay north of the county, with a Chan township.

translations.literal: Formerly Liang; Emperor Jing divided it off and established it.
translations.idiomatic: It had been Liang before Emperor Jing split it off.

translations.literal: Eight hundred ten li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It sat some eight hundred ten li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十城，户十万九千八百九十八，口六十万六千九十一。

translations.literal: Ten walled places; 109,898 households; 606,091 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Ten county seats, 109,898 households, and 606,091 inhabitants were registered.

translations.literal: Changyi: seat of the regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi served as the residence of the inspector for this province.

translations.literal: It had Liangqiu city.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqiu city appears in the record.

sentences.zh: 有甲父亭。杜預曰甲父，古國名，在縣東南。左傳隱十年「取防」，杜預曰縣西有防城。

translations.literal: It had Jiafu Pavilion. Du Yu says Jiafu was the name of an ancient state, southeast of the county. In Duke Yin 10, the Zuo Tradition says, “took Fang”; Du Yu says west of the county was Fang city.
translations.idiomatic: Jiafu Pavilion is also named. Du Yu explains that Jiafu was an ancient state southeast of the county, and when the Zuo Tradition records in Duke Yin 10 that they “took Fang,” he places Fang city west of the county.

sentences.zh: 〖东缗〗春秋时曰缗。左傳僖二十三年齊圍緡。

translations.literal: Dongmin: in the Spring and Autumn period it was called Min. In Duke Xi 23, the Zuo Tradition says Qi surrounded Min.
translations.idiomatic: Dongmin had been called simply Min in the Spring and Autumn period; the Zuo Tradition records Qi surrounding Min in Duke Xi 23.

sentences.zh: 〖钜野〗左傳桓七年「焚咸丘」，杜預曰縣西有咸亭。有大野澤。春秋西狩獲麟之所。爾雅十藪，魯有大野。杜預曰縣西南有郥亭。定十三年齊伐晉之所。

translations.literal: Juye: in Duke Huan 7, the Zuo Tradition says, “burned Xianqiu”; Du Yu says west of the county was Xian Pavilion. It had Daye Marsh. It was the place where the lin was captured on the western hunt in the Spring and Autumn. Among the ten marshes in the Erya, Lu had Daye. Du Yu says southwest of the county was Que Pavilion. It was the place where Qi attacked Jin in Duke Ding 13.
translations.idiomatic: At Juye, the Zuo Tradition records in Duke Huan 7 that someone “burned Xianqiu,” which Du Yu locates as Xian Pavilion west of the county. Juye contained Daye Marsh, the place where the lin was captured on the western hunt in the Spring and Autumn period; the Erya lists Daye among the ten marshes and assigns it to Lu. Du Yu also places Que Pavilion southwest of the county, the site where Qi attacked Jin in Duke Ding 13.

translations.literal: Gaoping: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping was organized as a marquisate.

translations.literal: Formerly Tuo; renamed by Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The place had been called Tuo until Emperor Zhang altered the name.

translations.literal: It had Mao Township city.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Township city stood in its borders.

translations.literal: Hulu: formerly Huling; renamed by Emperor Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu was the old Huling, which Emperor Zhang redesignated.

translations.literal: Nanpingyang: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Nanpingyang held marquisate status.

translations.literal: It had Qi Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition records the fortification of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: It had Qi Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition records the fortification of Qi.

sentences.zh: 有閭丘亭。左傳襄二十一年「邾庶其以漆、閭丘來奔」，杜預曰縣東北有漆鄕，西北有顯閭亭。哀七年囚邾子負瑕，杜預曰縣西北有瑕丘城。

translations.literal: It had Luqiu Pavilion. In Duke Xiang 21, the Zuo Tradition says, “Shuqi of Zhu came over with Qi and Luqiu”; Du Yu says the county had Qi Township to the northeast and Xianlu Pavilion to the northwest. In Duke Ai 7, when the viscount of Zhu, Fuxia, was imprisoned, Du Yu says Xiaqiu City was northwest of the county.
translations.idiomatic: It had Luqiu Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition says, “Shuqi of Zhu came over with Qi and Luqiu,” in Duke Xiang 21; Du Yu places Qi Township northeast of the county and Xianlu Pavilion northwest of it. For Duke Ai 7, when the viscount of Zhu, Fuxia, was imprisoned, Du Yu places Xiaqiu City northwest of the county.

sentences.zh: 〖方與〗有武唐亭，左傳桓二年盟於唐，杜預曰在西南。魯侯觀魚臺。春秋經隱五年矢魚於棠。

translations.literal: Fangyu had Wutang Pavilion. In Duke Huan 2, the Zuo Tradition says they covenanted at Tang; Du Yu says it was to the southwest. It had the terrace where the Marquis of Lu watched the fish. In Duke Yin 5, the Spring and Autumn Classic records shooting fish at Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu had Wutang Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition records a covenant at Tang in Duke Huan 2, and Du Yu places it to the southwest. It also had the terrace where the Marquis of Lu watched the fish; the Spring and Autumn Classic records shooting fish at Tang in Duke Yin 5.

translations.literal: It had Nimu Pavilion; some say it was the ancient Ningmu.
translations.idiomatic: Nimu Pavilion appears there, which some identify with old Ningmu.

translations.literal: Xiaqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqiu County.

sentences.zh: 〖金乡〗晉地道記曰：「縣多山，所治名金山。山北有鑿石爲冢，深十餘丈，隧長三十丈，傍卻入爲堂三方，雲得白兔不葬，更葬南山，鑿而得金，故曰金山。故冢今在。或云漢昌邑所作，或云秦時。」

translations.literal: Jinxiang: the Jin Didiao ji says, “The county had many mountains, and the seat was called Jinshan. North of the mountain, stone was cut to make a tomb, more than ten zhang deep, with a passage thirty zhang long, and side chambers entering off it on three sides. It is said that when a white rabbit was obtained they did not bury there, but buried instead on South Mountain; when they dug, they obtained gold, and therefore it was called Jinshan. The old tomb still survives. Some say it was made by Changyi of Han; some say it was from the Qin period.”
translations.idiomatic: For Jinxiang, the Jin Didiao ji says, “The county had many mountains, and the seat was called Jinshan. North of the mountain, stone had been cut into a tomb more than ten zhang deep, with a passage thirty zhang long and side chambers opening on three sides. It is said that after a white rabbit was found they did not bury there, but moved the burial to South Mountain; when they dug, they found gold, and so it was called Jinshan. The old tomb remains today. Some say Changyi of Han made it; others say it dates to Qin.”

translations.literal: Fangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdong County.

translations.literal: The Jiyin commandery: formerly Liang; Emperor Jing split it off and established it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin Commandery was another slice of the former Liang heartland created under Emperor Jing.

translations.literal: Eight hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Its seat was about eight hundred li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一城，户十三万三千七百一十五，口六十五万七千五百五十四。

translations.literal: Eleven walled places; 133,715 households; 657,554 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven county seats, 133,715 households, and 657,554 people fell under its administration.

sentences.zh: 〖定陶〗本曹国，郭璞曰：「城中有陶丘。」皇覽曰：「伯樂冢縣東南一里所，髙四五丈。」古陶，尧所居。帝王世記曰：「舜陶河濱，縣西南陶丘亭是。」

translations.literal: Dingtao: originally the state of Cao. Guo Pu says, “Inside the city was Taoqiu.” The Huanglan says, “Bo Le's tomb was about one li southeast of the county, four or five zhang high.” It was ancient Tao, where Yao dwelt. The Diwang shiji says, “Shun made pottery by the riverbank; Taoqiu Pavilion southwest of the county is this place.”
translations.idiomatic: Dingtao had been the state of Cao. Guo Pu says, “Inside the city was Taoqiu,” and the Huanglan says, “Bo Le's tomb was about one li southeast of the county, four or five zhang high.” This was ancient Tao, where Yao lived. The Diwang shiji says, “Shun made pottery by the riverbank; Taoqiu Pavilion southwest of the county is this place.”

sentences.zh: 有三鬷亭。湯伐三鬷，孔安國曰今定陶。

translations.literal: It had Sanzong Pavilion. Tang attacked Sanzong; Kong Anguo says this is present-day Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: Sanzong Pavilion is named in the same entry. Tang's campaign against Sanzong is glossed by Kong Anguo as taking place at present-day Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 〖冤句〗有煮枣城。史記蘇秦説魏襄王曰：「大王之地，東有淮、潁、煮棗。」

translations.literal: Yuanqu: it had Zhuzao city. In the Shiji, Su Qin says when persuading King Xiang of Wei, “Your Majesty's territory has Huai, Ying, and Zhuzao in the east.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqu contained the walled place called Zhuzao. In the Shiji, Su Qin tells King Xiang of Wei, “Your Majesty's territory has Huai, Ying, and Zhuzao in the east.”

sentences.zh: 〖成阳〗有尧冢、灵台，有雷泽。禹貢曰：「雷夏旣澤。」帝王世記曰：「舜耕歴山，漁雷澤，濟陰有歴山。」

translations.literal: Chengyang: it had Yao's tomb, the Spirit Terrace, and Lei Marsh. The Yugong says, “Leixia had become a marsh.” The Diwang shiji says, “Shun plowed at Mount Li and fished at Lei Marsh; Jiyin has Mount Li.”
translations.idiomatic: Chengyang held Yao's burial mound, the Spirit Terrace, and Lei Marsh. The Yugong says, “Leixia had become a marsh,” and the Diwang shiji says, “Shun plowed at Mount Li and fished at Lei Marsh; Jiyin has Mount Li.”

translations.literal: Chengshi: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi was organized as a marquisate.

translations.literal: It had the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: The Si River crossed the county.

translations.literal: It had Lucheng Township.
translations.idiomatic: Lucheng Township appears in the gazetteer.

translations.literal: Gouyang: it had Chui Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Gouyang had Chui Pavilion.

translations.literal: Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Juancheng County.

translations.literal: Lihu: formerly it belonged to Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lihu had once been part of Dong Commandery.

translations.literal: Linqiu: formerly it belonged to Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Linqiu, too, had been under Dong Commandery.

translations.literal: It had Gaoyu city.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyu city stood in the county.

translations.literal: It had Yuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng is also recorded.

translations.literal: Shanfu: a marquisate, formerly part of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shanfu was a marquisate transferred from Shanyang Commandery.

translations.literal: Chengwu: formerly it belonged to Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chengwu had previously been administered with Shanyang.

translations.literal: It had Gao city.
translations.idiomatic: The old city of Gao lay within its bounds.

translations.literal: Jishi: formerly it belonged to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi had once belonged to Liang.

sentences.zh: 右兗州刺史部，郡、国八，县、邑、公、侯国八十。

translations.literal: The foregoing completes the Yanzhou inspector’s circuit—eight commanderies and kingdoms and eighty county-level seats in all.
translations.idiomatic: Together these units made up the Yanzhou inspectorate: eight commanderies and kingdoms and eighty counties, towns, and marquisates.

sentences.zh: 东海郡高帝置，雒阳东千五百里。

translations.literal: The Donghai commandery was established by Emperor Gao; it lies fifteen hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai Commandery, founded under Emperor Gao, stretched about fifteen hundred li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户十四万八千七百八十四，口七十万六千四百一十六。

translations.literal: Thirteen walled places; 148,784 households; 706,416 persons.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised thirteen county seats, 148,784 households, and 706,416 inhabitants.

translations.literal: Tan: the native state; seat of the regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was the commandery’s own seat and the inspector’s residence.

sentences.zh: 〖兰陵〗有次室亭。地道記曰：「故魯次室邑。」列女傳有漆室之女，或作「次室」。

translations.literal: Lanling: it had Cishi Pavilion. The Didiao ji says, “It was the old Lu settlement of Cishi.” The Lienü zhuan has the woman of Qishi, sometimes written “Cishi.”
translations.idiomatic: Lanling contained Cishi Pavilion. The Didiao ji says, “It was the old Lu settlement of Cishi,” and the Lienü zhuan's woman of Qishi is sometimes written “Cishi.”

translations.literal: Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi County.

sentences.zh: 〖朐〗山海經曰：「都州在海中，一曰郁州。」郭璞曰：「在縣界。世俗傳此山在蒼梧徙來，上皆有南方樹木。」博物記：「縣東北海邊植石，秦所立之東門。」有铁。

translations.literal: Qu: the Shanhai jing says, “Duzhou is in the sea; one name is Yuzhou.” Guo Pu says, “It is within the county's bounds. Common tradition says this mountain moved here from Cangwu, and all the trees on it are southern trees.” The Bowu ji says, “The standing stones on the seashore northeast of the county were the eastern gate erected by Qin.” It had iron.
translations.idiomatic: For Qu, the Shanhai jing says, “Duzhou is in the sea; one name is Yuzhou.” Guo Pu places it within the county and says, “Common tradition says this mountain moved here from Cangwu, and all the trees on it are southern trees.” The Bowu ji adds, “The standing stones on the seashore northeast of the county were the eastern gate erected by Qin.” Qu was also an iron-producing county.

sentences.zh: 有伊卢乡。史記曰，鍾離昧家在伊盧。

translations.literal: It had Yilu Township. The Shiji says Zhongli Mo's family was at Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu Township lay in the same county; the Shiji says Zhongli Mo's family was there.

translations.literal: Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangben County.

sentences.zh: 〖昌虑〗有蓝乡。左傳昭三十一年邾黑肱以濫來奔，杜預曰縣所治，城東北有郳城。郳，小邾國也。

translations.literal: Changlü: it had Lan Township. In Duke Zhao 31, the Zuo Tradition says Zhu's Heigong came over with Lan; Du Yu says this was where the county seat was, and northeast of the city was Ni city. Ni was the state of Xiao Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Changlü held Lan Township. The Zuo Tradition records in Duke Zhao 31 that Heigong of Zhu came over with Lan; Du Yu identifies this with the county seat and notes Ni city northeast of the city, Ni being the state of Xiao Zhu.

translations.literal: Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng County.

translations.literal: Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yinping County.

translations.literal: Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng County.

translations.literal: Hexiang: the Guo River runs south from here to Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: At Hexiang, the Guo River runs southward from here to Hulu.

sentences.zh: 〖祝其〗有羽山，殛鯀之山。杜預曰在縣西南。博物記曰：「東北獨居山，西南有淵水，卽羽泉也，俗謂此山爲懲父山。」

translations.literal: Zhuqi: it had Mount Yu, the mountain where Gun was executed. Du Yu says it was southwest of the county. The Bowu ji says, “To the northeast stands Dujushan; to the southwest is Yuanshui, which is Yuquan. Commonly this mountain is called Chengfu Mountain.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuqi contained Mount Yu, remembered as the mountain where Gun was executed. Du Yu places it southwest of the county. The Bowu ji says, “To the northeast stands Dujushan; to the southwest is Yuanshui, which is Yuquan. Commonly this mountain is called Chengfu Mountain.”

sentences.zh: 春秋时曰祝其，夹谷地。左傳定十年會齊侯夾谷，孔子相。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn period it was called Zhuqi, the ground of Jiagu. In Duke Ding 10, the Zuo Tradition says there was a meeting with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu, and Confucius served as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In Spring and Autumn times the place was known as Zhuqi, the Jiagu site; the Zuo Tradition records a meeting there with the Marquis of Qi in Duke Ding 10, with Confucius acting as assistant.

sentences.zh: 〖厚丘〗左傳成九年「城中城」，杜預曰在縣西南，有中鄕城。

translations.literal: Houqiu: in Duke Cheng 9, the Zuo Tradition says, “walled Zhongcheng”; Du Yu says it was southwest of the county and had Zhongxiang city.
translations.idiomatic: For Houqiu, the Zuo Tradition records in Duke Cheng 9 that they “walled Zhongcheng”; Du Yu places it southwest of the county and notes Zhongxiang city there.

sentences.zh: 〖赣榆〗本属琅邪，建初五年复。左傳「齊伐莒，莒子奔紀鄣」，杜預曰縣東北有紀城。地道記曰：「海中去岸百五十歩，有秦始皇碑，長一丈八尺，廣五尺，厚八尺三寸；一行十二字。潮水至加其上三丈，去則三尺見也。」

translations.literal: Ganyu: originally it belonged to Langye; restored in the fifth year of Jianchu. The Zuo Tradition says, “Qi attacked Ju, and the Viscount of Ju fled to Jizhang”; Du Yu says northeast of the county was Ji city. The Didiao ji says, “In the sea, one hundred fifty paces from the shore, there is a stele of Qin Shi Huang, one zhang eight chi long, five chi wide, and eight chi three cun thick; each line has twelve characters. When the tide comes in, it rises three zhang above it; when the tide withdraws, three chi of it can be seen.”
translations.idiomatic: Ganyu had belonged to Langye until it was restored in Jianchu 5. The Zuo Tradition says, “Qi attacked Ju, and the Viscount of Ju fled to Jizhang,” which Du Yu identifies with Ji city northeast of the county. The Didiao ji says, “In the sea, one hundred fifty paces from the shore, there is a stele of Qin Shi Huang, one zhang eight chi long, five chi wide, and eight chi three cun thick; each line has twelve characters. When the tide comes in, it rises three zhang above it; when the tide withdraws, three chi of it can be seen.”

translations.literal: The Langye kingdom was established by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Langye Kingdom was established by Qin.

sentences.zh: 建武中省城阳国，以其县属。

translations.literal: During Jianwu the Chengyang kingdom was abolished and its counties were attached.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era the Chengyang kingdom was struck off and its counties folded in here.

translations.literal: One thousand five hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom lay fifteen hundred li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十三城，户二万八百四，口五十七万九百六十七。

translations.literal: Thirteen walled places; 20,804 households; 570,967 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen seats, 20,804 households, and 570,967 people completed its rolls.

sentences.zh: 〖开阳〗杜預曰古鄅。左傳哀三年城啓陽，杜預曰開陽。故属东海，建初五年属。

translations.literal: Kaiyang: Du Yu says it was ancient Yu. In Duke Ai 3, the Zuo Tradition says they walled Qiyang; Du Yu says this was Kaiyang. Formerly it belonged to Donghai; attached in the fifth year of Jianchu.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyang, Du Yu says, was ancient Yu. When the Zuo Tradition records the walling of Qiyang in Duke Ai 3, Du Yu identifies it as Kaiyang. It had belonged to Donghai until Jianchu 5, when it was transferred here.

translations.literal: Dongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Dongwu County.

sentences.zh: 〖琅邪〗山海經雲有琅邪臺，在勃海閒，琅邪之東。郭璞曰：「琅邪臨海邊，有山嶕嶢特起，狀如髙臺。此卽琅邪臺。」齊景公曰：「吾循海而南，放乎琅邪。」越絶曰：「句踐徙琅邪，起觀臺，臺周七里，以望東海。」史記曰秦始皇徙黔首三萬戸琅邪臺下。傳有勞山。

translations.literal: Langye: the Shanhai jing says it had Langye Terrace, between the Bohai and east of Langye. Guo Pu says, “Langye faces the seashore, where a mountain rises steep and high like a tall terrace. This is Langye Terrace.” Duke Jing of Qi said, “I follow the sea south and wander at Langye.” The Yuejue says, “Goujian moved to Langye and built a viewing terrace; the terrace was seven li around, from which he looked out over the Eastern Sea.” The Shiji says Qin Shi Huang moved thirty thousand households of commoners below Langye Terrace. Tradition says it had Mount Lao.
translations.idiomatic: For Langye, the Shanhai jing says that Langye Terrace stood between the Bohai and east of Langye. Guo Pu says, “Langye faces the seashore, where a mountain rises steep and high like a tall terrace. This is Langye Terrace.” Duke Jing of Qi said, “I follow the sea south and wander at Langye.” The Yuejue says, “Goujian moved to Langye and built a viewing terrace; the terrace was seven li around, from which he looked out over the Eastern Sea.” The Shiji adds that Qin Shi Huang moved thirty thousand households of commoners below Langye Terrace; tradition also notes Mount Lao.

translations.literal: Dongguan: it had Yun Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition says, “The duke resided at Yun.”
translations.idiomatic: Dongguan held Yun Pavilion; the Zuo Tradition says, “The duke resided at Yun.”

translations.literal: It had Pi Township.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Township appears in the same note.

translations.literal: It had Mount Gonglai.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Gonglai rose in the county.

sentences.zh: 或曰古浮来。左傳隱八年盟浮來，杜預曰邳來山之閒，號曰邳來。莊九年鮑叔受管仲，及堂阜而脱之。杜預曰：「東莞蒙陰縣西北有夷吾亭，或曰鮑叔解夷吾縛於此，因以爲名。」卽古堂阜也，東莞後爲郡。

translations.literal: Some say it was ancient Fulai. In Duke Yin 8, the Zuo Tradition records a covenant at Fulai; Du Yu says it was between the Pilai mountains and was called Pilai. In Duke Zhuang 9, Bao Shu received Guan Zhong and released him when they reached Tangfu. Du Yu says, “Northwest of Mengyin county in Dongguan was Yiwu Pavilion; some say Bao Shu released Yiwu from his bonds here, and for this reason it was named.” This was ancient Tangfu; Dongguan later became a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Some authorities identify the peak with old Fulai. The Zuo Tradition records a covenant at Fulai in Duke Yin 8, which Du Yu places between the Pilai mountains and says was called Pilai. In Duke Zhuang 9, Bao Shu received Guan Zhong and released him at Tangfu; Du Yu says, “Northwest of Mengyin county in Dongguan was Yiwu Pavilion; some say Bao Shu released Yiwu from his bonds here, and for this reason it was named.” This was old Tangfu, and Dongguan later became a commandery.

sentences.zh: 〖西海〗東觀書曰有勝山。博物記：「太公呂望所出，今有東呂鄕。又釣於棘津，其浦今存。」

translations.literal: Xihai: the Dongguan Hanji says it had Mount Sheng. The Bowu ji says, “This is where Grand Duke Lü Wang came from; today there is Donglü Township. He also fished at Jijin, and its inlet still survives.”
translations.idiomatic: At Xihai, the Dongguan Hanji notes Mount Sheng. The Bowu ji says, “This is where Grand Duke Lü Wang came from; today there is Donglü Township. He also fished at Jijin, and its inlet still survives.”

sentences.zh: 〖诸〗左傳莊二十九年「城諸」，杜預曰諸縣在城陽郡。又隱四年「莒人伐杞，取牟婁」，杜預曰縣東北有婁鄕。

translations.literal: Zhu: in Duke Zhuang 29, the Zuo Tradition says, “walled Zhu”; Du Yu says Zhu county was in Chengyang Commandery. Again, in Duke Yin 4, it says, “The men of Ju attacked Qi and took Moulou”; Du Yu says northeast of the county was Lou Township.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhu, the Zuo Tradition records in Duke Zhuang 29 that they “walled Zhu,” and Du Yu places Zhu county in Chengyang Commandery. In Duke Yin 4 it says, “The men of Ju attacked Qi and took Moulou,” which Du Yu connects with Lou Township northeast of the county.

translations.literal: Ju: the native state; formerly it belonged to Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was the kingdom’s seat and had once lain under Chengyang’s administration.

translations.literal: It had iron.
translations.idiomatic: Iron was mined in the county.

translations.literal: It had Zhengrong Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengrong Valley cut through its hills.

translations.literal: Dong'an: formerly it belonged to Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong’an had earlier been part of Chengyang Commandery.

translations.literal: Yangdu: formerly it belonged to Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yangdu, too, had once been filed under Chengyang.

translations.literal: It had Mou Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Terrace overlooked the same district.

translations.literal: Linyi: formerly it belonged to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi had previously belonged to Donghai Commandery.

translations.literal: It had Cong Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Pavilion stood in the county.

sentences.zh: 〖即丘〗侯国，故属东海，春秋曰祝丘。

translations.literal: Jiqiu: a marquisate, formerly part of Donghai; in the Spring and Autumn period it was called Zhuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqiu was a marquisate taken from Donghai and known in the chronicles as Zhuqiu.

translations.literal: Zeng: a marquisate, formerly part of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng was another marquisate carved from old Donghai territory.

translations.literal: It had Gai Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Pavilion appears in the gazetteer.

translations.literal: Gumu.
translations.idiomatic: Gumu County.

sentences.zh: 彭城国高祖置为楚，章帝改。

translations.literal: The Pengcheng kingdom: Emperor Gao established it as Chu; Emperor Zhang changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao had first founded the kingdom as Chu until Emperor Zhang redesignated it Pengcheng.

translations.literal: One thousand two hundred twenty li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital lay about twelve hundred twenty li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 八城，户八万六千一百七十，口四十九万三千二十七。

translations.literal: Eight walled places; 86,170 households; 493,027 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eight county seats, 86,170 households, and 493,027 inhabitants were counted.

sentences.zh: 〖彭城〗古大彭邑。北征記城西二十里有山，山有楚元王墓。伏滔北征記曰：「城北六里有山，臨泗，有宋桓魋石槨，皆靑石，隱起龜龍鱗鳳之象。」有铁。

translations.literal: Pengcheng: it was the ancient settlement of Great Peng. The Beizheng ji says that twenty li west of the city was a mountain, and on the mountain was the tomb of King Yuan of Chu. Fu Tao's Beizheng ji says, “Six li north of the city was a mountain, facing the Si River, with Song Huan Tui's stone outer coffin. All the stones were blue, with raised images of turtles, dragons, scales, and phoenixes.” It had iron.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng was the ancient settlement of Great Peng. The Beizheng ji says a mountain twenty li west of the city held the tomb of King Yuan of Chu. Fu Tao's Beizheng ji says, “Six li north of the city was a mountain, facing the Si River, with Song Huan Tui's stone outer coffin. All the stones were blue, with raised images of turtles, dragons, scales, and phoenixes.” Pengcheng was also an iron-working county.

translations.literal: Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan County.

sentences.zh: 〖傅阳〗有柤水。左傳襄十年滅偪陽，杜預曰卽此縣也。

translations.literal: Fuyang: it had the Zha River. In Duke Xiang 10, the Zuo Tradition says Biyang was extinguished; Du Yu says this was this county.
translations.idiomatic: The Zha River flowed through Fuyang. The Zuo Tradition records Biyang's destruction in Duke Xiang 10, which Du Yu identifies with this county.

translations.literal: Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Lü County.

translations.literal: Liu: the Xizheng ji says inside the city was Zhang Liang's temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu, the Xizheng ji notes Zhang Liang's temple within the city.

translations.literal: Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu County.

translations.literal: Ziqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqiu County.

translations.literal: Guangqi: formerly it belonged to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi had once been administered from Pei.

sentences.zh: 广陵郡景帝置为江都，武帝更名。

translations.literal: The Guangling commandery: Emperor Jing established it as Jiangdu; Emperor Wu changed the name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing first organized the area as Jiangdu until Emperor Wu renamed it Guangling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 建武中省泗水国，以其县属。

translations.literal: During Jianwu the Sishui kingdom was abolished and its counties were attached.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu’s Jianwu reign the Sishui kingdom was struck off and its counties merged in here.

sentences.zh: 雒阳东一千六百四十里。

translations.literal: One thousand six hundred forty li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery sat some sixteen hundred forty li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一城，户八万三千九百七，口四十一万一百九十。

translations.literal: Eleven walled places; 83,907 households; 410,190 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven seats, 83,907 households, and 410,190 people were registered.

translations.literal: Guangling: it had Dongling Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling contained Dongling Pavilion.

translations.literal: Jiangdu: it had a shrine to the Yangtze River.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangdu maintained a cult hall for the great river.

translations.literal: Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyou County.

translations.literal: Ping’an.
translations.idiomatic: Ping’an County.

translations.literal: Ling: formerly it belonged to Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Ling had once been part of the Sishui kingdom.

translations.literal: Dongyang: formerly it belonged to Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyang had previously been Linhuai territory.

sentences.zh: 有長洲澤，吳王濞太倉在此。縣多麋。博物記曰：「千千爲群，掘食草根，其處成泥，名曰麋畯。民人隨此畯種稻，不耕而穫，其收百倍。」又扶海洲上有草名蒒，其實食之如大麥，從七月稔熟，民斂穫至冬乃訖，名曰自然穀，或曰禹餘糧。

translations.literal: It had Changzhou Marsh, and King Bi of Wu’s great granary was located there. The county had many moose. The Bowu ji says, “They gather in herds of thousands, dig up and eat grass roots, and the places where they do so become mud, called moose furrows. The people follow these furrows to plant rice, and without plowing they harvest it, with yields one hundredfold.” Also, on Fuhai Island there was a grass named shi; its seed was eaten like barley, ripening from the seventh month, and the people gathered it until winter ended. It was called natural grain, or Yu’s surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: It had Changzhou Marsh, where King Bi of Wu kept his great granary. The county had many moose. The Bowu ji says, “They gather in herds of thousands, dig up and eat grass roots, and the places where they do so become mud, called moose furrows. The people follow these furrows to plant rice, and without plowing they harvest it, with yields one hundredfold.” On Fuhai Island there was also a grass called shi; its seed was eaten like barley, ripened from the seventh month, and was gathered by the people until winter ended. It was called natural grain, or Yu’s surplus grain.

translations.literal: Sheyang: formerly it belonged to Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Sheyang had also been under Linhuai.

translations.literal: Yandu: formerly it belonged to Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Yandu was another county transferred from Linhuai.

translations.literal: Yu: a marquisate, formerly part of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a marquisate taken from Linhuai.

translations.literal: Tangyi: formerly it belonged to Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Tangyi had once been administered with Linhuai.

translations.literal: It had iron.
translations.idiomatic: The county produced iron.

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn period it was called Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn records knew the place simply as Tang.

translations.literal: Haixi: formerly it belonged to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi had belonged to Donghai Commandery before the reorganization.

sentences.zh: 下邳国武帝置为临淮郡，永平十五年更为下邳国。

translations.literal: The Xiapi kingdom: Emperor Wu established it as Linhuai Commandery; in the fifteenth year of Yongping it became the Xiapi kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had first set the region up as Linhuai Commandery, and in 72 CE, Yongping 15, it was elevated to the kingdom of Xiapi.

translations.literal: One thousand four hundred li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It stood about fourteen hundred li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十七城，户十三万六千三百八十九，口六十一万一千八十三。

translations.literal: Seventeen walled places; 136,389 households; 611,083 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen county seats, 136,389 households, and 611,083 subjects completed its rolls.

translations.literal: Xiapi: originally it belonged to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiapi had once been a Donghai county.

translations.literal: It had Mount Geyi, originally called Yiyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Geyi rose there, once known as Yiyang Mountain.

translations.literal: It had iron.
translations.idiomatic: Iron was mined in the county.

translations.literal: Xu: the native state.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was the kingdom’s own ancient seat.

translations.literal: It had Lou Pavilion; some say it was the ancient Loulin.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Pavilion is named there, which some identify with old Loulin.

translations.literal: Tong: a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was organized as a marquisate.

translations.literal: Suiling.
translations.idiomatic: Suiling County.

translations.literal: Xiaxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaxiang County.

translations.literal: Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin County.

translations.literal: Huaipu.
translations.idiomatic: Huaipu County.

translations.literal: Xutai.
translations.idiomatic: Xutai County.

translations.literal: Gaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoshan County.

translations.literal: Panjing.
translations.idiomatic: Panjing County.

translations.literal: Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: Huailing County.

translations.literal: Qulü: it had the Pugu marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Qulü contained the Pugu marshlands.

translations.literal: Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dongcheng County.

translations.literal: Quyang: a marquisate, formerly part of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Quyang was a marquisate transferred from Donghai.

translations.literal: Siwu: a marquisate, formerly part of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Siwu was another marquisate once under Donghai.

translations.literal: Liangcheng: formerly it belonged to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Liangcheng had been Donghai territory.

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn period it was called Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicles record the old name Liang.

translations.literal: Xiaqiu: formerly it belonged to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqiu had once been part of Pei.

sentences.zh: 右徐州刺史部，郡、国五，县、邑、侯国六十二。

translations.literal: The foregoing completes the Xuzhou inspector’s circuit—five commanderies and kingdoms, sixty-two counties, towns, and marquisates in all.
translations.idiomatic: These entries close the Xuzhou inspectorate: five commanderies and kingdoms and sixty-two county-level seats altogether.
